title: How long to see every face?
hook: A die has six faces. So six rolls, give or take, should show you all of them. Right?

knows: a fair die shows each face with chance 1/6
doesNotKnow: that the wait for a new face grows as fewer faces are missing
the coupon collector total of about 14.7 rolls

misconception: Rolling a die six times shows each face about once, so seeing all six takes about 6 rolls.
objective: The learner can explain that each new face gets harder to find (with k faces missing, only k rolls in 6 help), so the waits are 1, 1.2, 1.5, 2, 3 and 6 rolls on average, 14.7 in all, and the last face is the expensive one.

claims.text: On average it takes 14.7 rolls of a fair die to see all six faces.
claims.source: Sum of geometric waits: 6/6 + 6/5 + 6/4 + 6/3 + 6/2 + 6/1 = 6 x H_6 = 6 x 2.45 = 14.7 (expectedTotal in src/demos/probability/collect-all-six-faces/model.ts). Reference: W. Feller, An Introduction to Probability Theory and Its Applications, Vol. 1, 3rd ed. (1968), waiting times in sampling (the coupon collector's problem); chapter not checked by the builder.

claims.text: With one face missing, only 1 roll in 6 helps, so the last face alone takes 6 rolls on average; the waits for each new face are 1, 1.2, 1.5, 2, 3 and 6 rolls.
claims.source: With k faces still missing a roll succeeds with chance k/6; a geometric wait with success chance p has mean 1/p = 6/k (expectedWaits in model.ts).

claims.text: Over the stage's 1,000 simulated collections the average was 14.9 rolls, with average waits 1, 1.23, 1.50, 2.04, 2.85 and 6.25.
claims.source: many() in model.ts, seed 6000, untuned (the first seed tried). Over 200 other seeds the 1,000-collection average ranged 14.18-15.26 (median 14.74). The first stage collection (seed 600) takes 12 rolls.

claims.text: Only 13 of the 1,000 collections finished in six rolls; the exact chance is about 1.5%.
claims.source: Six rolls showing six different faces: 6!/6^6 = 720/46,656 = 0.0154. The 13 is from many() (within6).

recall.question: You are collecting 10 different stickers, each pack has one at random. You have 9. On average, how many more packs until the last one?
recall.why: Only 1 sticker in 10 is new, so the wait averages 10 packs. The last item of a collection is the expensive one.
